soft_deny: Bash(kamal deploy:*) in ~/apps/SubmittalKit: production deploy via Kamal, scope to explicit confirmation

make prod-db-console, db-destroy, db-drop and db-reset targets in any repo's Makefile: destructive or production-scoped database operations
environment: ### Org-wide

**Secrets management**: SubmittalKit keeps deploy secrets in .kamal/secrets and bin/prod-secret. The dotfiles repo uses Ansible Vault. Other repos: none configured
**Default / protected branches**: main in SubmittalKit and dotfiles, with no rulesets or protected-branch rules. Treat any repo as unprotected unless told otherwise
**CI/CD deploy targets**: SubmittalKit deploys with Kamal (Makefile `deploy`, `prod-db-console` and `env-unlive` targets). Other repos: none configured
**Network posture**: None configured
**Source control**: Any repo whose origin remote is under github.com/JeremyDwayne, pushed to that origin only. No other orgs configured
**Trusted internal domains**: submittalkit.com
**Trusted cloud buckets**: None configured
**Key internal services**: None configured
**Internal package registry**: None configured

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: In any repo: .env, .env.*, *.pem, *.key. In SubmittalKit also .kamal/secrets, bin/prod-secret and prod-slow-queries.txt. These hold credentials and production data; share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar
**Data retention / declassification**: None configured
**Sensitive remote targets**: prod-slow-queries (k8s namespace flag seen 1×), prod-db-console (Makefile target), any namespace/host/container with `prod`/`production` as a whole word or name segment
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: None configured — fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment

**Trusted repos**: the user's own repos under github.com/JeremyDwayne and their origin remotes. Confidential non-secret business data is fine to commit and push to the private ones only; public repos get nothing confidential. Routine in SubmittalKit under the submittalkit/ prefix: Django app code, templates, and migrations
